docs.title: pynxtools-xrm
docs.text: pynxtools-xrm converts ZEISS X-ray microscopy data into NeXus and integrates the conversion with NOMAD Oasis. ZBT – Zentrum für BrennstoffzellenTechnik GmbH develops this community plugin through Jonas Fortmann (j.formtann@zbt.de). It is not authored or maintained by “The NOMAD Authors”. NOMAD, pynxtools and the NeXus definitions are upstream projects and retain their own authorship.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Install the package in the intended environment.
  2. For a server, complete Oasis deployment, including definition preparation and environment variables for all workers.
  3. Follow the upload guide to preserve directory structure and make image-to-metadata associations unambiguous.
  4. Supply genuine missing values using additional metadata.
  5. Check each image and generated NeXus entry; a completed upload does not imply that every entry succeeded. See troubleshooting.

docs.title: Supported conversions
docs.text:
Data Application Initiation TXRM projections NXtomo Automatic ZEISS binary parser TXM reconstruction NXtomoproc Automatic ZEISS binary parser Single-image XRM Local NXxrm_image Automatic ZEISS binary parser Numbered grayscale TIFF stack NXtomoproc or NXtomo YAML job or CLI

Each binary image owns one output. RCP files provide associated recipe metadata; they do not independently produce converted image entries. The local NXxrm_tomoproc XML is not an active conversion target in this implementation.

docs.title: Architecture and operation
docs.text:
Developed at ZBT by Jonas Fortmann. For operational steps use the deployment guide, upload guide and output reference.

All conversion entry points call streaming_writer.convert. XRMReader remains a pynxtools MultiFormatReader; format inspection and metadata mapping are separate from the pixel phase. ZeissSource reads the OLE directory and small header streams, then opens one image stream at a time. TiffSource adapts the existing TIFF manifest. No complete pixel volume is assembled. Header arrays and the OLE directory grow with frame count, so total metadata memory is not constant.

The standard pynxtools Writer creates metadata using the selected NXDL. Links to pixels are deferred until the HDF5 adapter has created their targets. Each frame is written to a fixed-size gzip dataset. Float reference images remain in separate NXdata groups with their original datatype. All non-image vendor streams and complete associated recipes are retained as base64 JSON in NXnote datasets. This preserves metadata stream bytes; it does not preserve the original OLE file layout or embed a byte-identical copy of the entire image file.

Output creation uses an exclusive per-output lock, a temporary file, NXDL and shape checks, and atomic replacement. Failed conversions preserve an existing valid output. Repeated conversion can reuse a validated result when source path/size/mtime, effective metadata, recipe, compression, application NXDL and implementation fingerprint match. The source pixel SHA-256 is recorded during writing; cache lookup uses file stamps rather than rereading gigabytes of pixels.

Input Dataset order Write operation TXRM / projection TIFF frame, column, row data[i] = frame.T TXM / reconstruction TIFF x, y-layer, z data[:, i, :] = frame.T XRM row, column data[:, :] = frame

TXM requires explicit image_orientation (row_axis=z, column_axis=x, signs +/-1). Its measured Y positions are checked against the single cubic voxel size. X/Z axes are local centered pixel offsets; the volume is related to the native sample frame through the stored stage transformations. TIFF volumes additionally require volume_origin_um, the first voxel coordinate in that frame. Raw TIFFs require a real theta array and one image_key per frame. No uniform angle series is generated. XRM pixel axes are local row/column distances with no asserted orientation in stage coordinates.

The global coordinate system uses X along the beam, source -X and detector +X, Y down, and right-handed Z. The sample basis is B @ Ry(theta), with B=[[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[-1,0,0]]. Native translations depend on the rotation chain. NXcoordinate_system explicitly relates this global frame to the NeXus default. Detector layout=area and type='planar area detector' record the user-confirmed geometry. Sensor pitch is never substituted for object-side pixel size.

docs.title: NOMAD deployment
docs.text:
Install the package into the app/worker environment to register xrm_raw_parser. Prepare an overlay with pynx-xrm definitions --output run/xrm-definitions. Set NEXUS_DEF_PATH to its absolute path before starting every app/worker process, and restart after plugin entry-point changes. The overlay is a copy of the installed definitions plus NXxrm_image; third-party package files are untouched. Its marker records the base revision and custom application checksum.

The binary MatchingParser checks extension, compound-file signature and ZEISS image headers without converting. The image mainfile owns conversion; an optional archive.yaml points at it with input_file and requests that owner to reprocess. Generated files use _nexus/<relative path>/<original name including extension>.nxs. Their processing is requested through NOMAD's process_updated_raw_file interface. Reused outputs do not trigger another generated-file processing request.

RCP matching uses explicit RecipePoint file declarations and acquisition directory context. The nearest unambiguous eLabFTW scope is used. Multiple matching metadata files or recipes require explicit assignment. Server inputs must remain inside the upload root; original absolute ZEISS paths are retained only as provenance. Adding/changing RCP or JSON later requires reprocessing the upload. There is no custom sidecar watcher or hidden background conversion service.

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  tiff_directory: layers
  metadata_file: metadata.json
  target_definition: NXtomoproc
  output: result.nxs
  metadata_supplements:
    theta: 0
    stage_x_um: 0
    stage_y_um: 0
    stage_z_um: 0
    volume_origin_um: [-0.75, -0.5, -0.5]
    image_orientation: {row_axis: z, column_axis: x, row_sign: 1, column_sign: 1}

The geometry values above are a synthetic example, not defaults for measurements. Reconstruction program/version/date and source name/type must be supplied by genuine metadata.

docs.title: Definition scope
docs.text: The active targets are NXtomo, NXtomoproc and NXxrm_image. The optional packaged NXxrm_tomoproc extension is not an enabled target and is not copied into the overlay. See definition setup.

docs.title: Metadata mapping and strict validation
docs.text:
For concrete YAML/JSON examples, units, timestamps and file assignments see additional metadata. This reference describes the current implemented mapping, not all fields that a manufacturer file may contain.

Effective precedence is image > associated RCP > eLabFTW > explicit missing values. Conflicting lower-priority values remain in provenance. Explicit configuration cannot change an existing value. Invalid high-priority metadata are not replaced. RCP settings are preserved as recipe settings; nominal angle limits are never used to fabricate measured angle arrays. All RCP streams remain recoverable from entry/recipe/data (JSON with raw_streams_base64).

Required content NXtomo NXtomoproc NXxrm_image ZEISS source Sample name yes yes yes assigned RCP SampleName or ELN/config Image pixels / dimensions / datatype yes yes yes ImageInfo and ImageData blocks Theta and stage X/Y/Z profile profile profile Angles, X/Y/ZPosition; TXM MeanSampleX/Y/Z Rotation angle array / image_key yes no no measured Angles; primary TXRM projections key=0 Cubic object pixel/voxel size optional yes yes ImageInfo/PixelSize (um) Source name / type optional yes optional explicit proven source; numeric SourceType not decoded Reconstruction program/version/date no yes no ELN/config; TXM exeVersion retained separately, no layer-date fallback Raw acquisition file no yes no ReconSettings/InputFileName or assigned RCP Physical image orientation local axes yes local axes explicit calibrated row/column axes and signs Volume origin no TIFF required no explicit TIFF origin; measured TXM Y plus local X/Z offsets

The NXDL validator is authoritative for the pinned application contract. Profile requirements add geometry and provenance checks. Missing fields are reported together by MissingRequiredMetadata before output creation where possible.

Optional metadata Destination / handling XrayVoltage, XrayCurrent, ExpTimes NXsource voltage/current, detector count_time Acquisition ImageInfo/StoRADistance, DtoRADistance Signed X transformations in mm; never sample-center distance TXM ReconInputTomoParams/StoRADistance, DtoRADistance Positive magnitudes in um, converted to mm and placed on the confirmed global axis: source -X, detector +X. TXM ImageInfo distances are not decoded using the acquisition convention. CameraName, CameraSerialNumberString Detector description and serial_number ObjectiveName, SourceFilterName instrument/optics/objective and instrument/filter/description; manufacturer bytes retained ImageInfo/Date Berlin frame_times in provenance; first projection timestamp as start_time TXM ImageInfo/Date Layer timestamps retained; never asserted as reconstruction process time CamPixelSize Sensor pitch retained distinctly from object voxel/pixel calibration IsFlatPanel and unknown vendor fields Raw stream bytes with original OLE paths eLabFTW identity/project/sample/users/notes NXentry, NXsample, NXuser and NXnote Additional acquisition/reconstruction/storage fields Native scalar/array datasets in optional domain NXcollections; no serialized eLabFTW JSON

All full local timestamps use Europe/Berlin, with real UTC conversion for aware values. Full timestamp fields reject date-only strings, DST gaps and ambiguous local times. The optional acquisition/measurement_date preserves a calendar date without inventing a time. Original ZEISS bytes and the RCP recipe remain as provenance notes. Conversion time is the actual new conversion time and is distinct from acquisition/reconstruction time.

The eLabFTW field registry is maintained in elabftw.py. Standard NXsample, NXsource, NXdetector, NXfilter, NXuser, NXentry and NXprocess fields are used where their semantics match. Additional fields live in named domain NXcollections, which are optional base-class extensions rather than required application fields. Instrument item identifiers are resolved to names only through an exact linked record match. Multiselect text fields remain native UTF-8 arrays. Form settings, access control, history and UI fields have no verified domain destination and are listed individually in metadata_provenance/elabftw_mapping (source_path, target_path, status, reason). Empty fields are reported separately. Unknown populated extra fields retain their native value/unit under unmapped_metadata. The original eLabFTW JSON is not embedded, including in the provenance group. Lower-priority conflicting values and selected field origins are native datasets.

The single-image profile is a local application named NXxrm_image using generic NXimage and NXdata; it does not mislabel X-ray microscopy as electron microscopy through NXem. Its NXDL is packaged and added to an explicit definitions overlay.

docs.title: Source-reader limitations
docs.text: RCP decoding currently contributes SampleName and the acquisition reference (AcqFileName for NXtomoproc); other recipe streams are preserved but not automatically mapped into missing reconstruction/source fields. The eLabFTW resolver requires exact labels such as Source name, Source type, Reconstruction software, Software version and Reconstruction date under metadata_decoded.extra_fields. It does not query a live laboratory notebook. Orientation is read from explicit configuration. These implementation limits are distinct from fields being absent in the original data.

docs.title: Windows: ZIP upload requires a second processing run
docs.text: This is a historical development incident tied to the NOMAD revision cited below. Check your installed NOMAD version before assuming the same core defect. For current plugin setup failures see conversion troubleshooting.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
On a locally hosted NOMAD Oasis running on Windows, an uploaded ZIP archive can be extracted successfully but still leave the upload workflow in the failed state. Starting Reprocess a second time then succeeds.

This is not an error in XRMDataConverter or in the generated NXtomoproc file. The failure happens earlier, while NOMAD imports and removes the temporary ZIP archive. The observed exception is a Windows file-locking error:

PermissionError: [WinError 32]
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process:
.../.volumes/fs/tmp/<upload-id>/<upload>.zip

The problem was reproduced with both a small synthetic XRM upload and the complete AvCarb_FLEX_20bar.zip upload. It is relevant primarily to local Windows development. A production Oasis running on Linux is normally not blocked by this particular symptom because Linux permits unlinking an open file. The underlying file handle should nevertheless be closed explicitly.

docs.title: Observable processing sequence
docs.text:
The first workflow proceeds as follows:

  1. NOMAD receives the ZIP in its temporary upload directory.
  2. StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() recognizes and extracts the ZIP.
  3. All JSON, TIFF, and *.archive.yaml files are copied into the staging raw directory.
  4. NOMAD leaves the archive filesystem context.
  5. NOMAD attempts to delete the temporary ZIP.
  6. Windows rejects the deletion because the outer fsspec file handle is still open.
  7. The update_files_activity and therefore the first upload workflow fail.

The extracted files remain in staging despite that failure. During the second processing run NOMAD operates on these existing raw files, the archive parser loads the XRM entry, and XRMDataConverter.normalize() can produce and register the .nxs file successfully.

The important distinction is therefore:

First run:  ZIP import -> extraction -> temporary ZIP deletion fails
Second run: existing raw files -> archive parser -> XRM normalizer succeeds

docs.title: 1. NOMAD opens the archive with fsspec
docs.text:
The relevant context manager is FSUtility._open_archive_fs() in:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py

At NOMAD commit 2ddd7fb88711ab30b97b88a70c48e93be5b6ebd3, the local helper closes the archive filesystem after yielding it:

def _wrap(_fs):
    yield _fs
    if hasattr(_fs, "close"):
        _fs.close()

Reference: nomad/files.py in NOMAD

There are two issues with this implementation:

  • cleanup is not protected by try/finally, so an exception raised by the caller could bypass _fs.close();
  • ZipFileSystem.close() does not close the owning fsspec.core.OpenFile object that was opened when the ZIP filesystem was constructed from a path.

docs.title: 2. NOMAD extracts the ZIP
docs.text:
StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() opens the ZIP through FSUtility.open_archive() and copies all archive members:

if archive_format == "zip":
    with FSUtility.open_archive(path, fs=target_fs) as _fs:
        yield "", "", _fs

Local reference:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py:1766

docs.title: 3. NOMAD deletes the temporary source
docs.text:
After extraction, the same method removes the temporary upload file:

finally:
    if cleanup_source_file_and_dir:
        self._fs.rm(path, recursive=True)

Local reference:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py:1810

On Windows this removal raises PermissionError while the source ZIP still has an open handle.

docs.title: 4. fsspec keeps a separate owner object
docs.text:
When ZipFileSystem receives a path, its constructor creates an fsspec.core.OpenFile, enters that context, and stores both the owner and the opened file:

fo = fsspec.open(fo, mode=m, protocol=target_protocol, **target_options)
self.of = fo
self.fo = fo.__enter__()
self.zip = zipfile.ZipFile(self.fo, mode=mode, ...)

Its explicit close() method closes self.zip, while closing self.of is handled separately by the destructor. Garbage collection is not guaranteed to run before NOMAD tries to delete the temporary archive.

References:

  • fsspec ZipFileSystem
  • fsspec OpenFile

docs.title: Why XRMDataConverter is not the cause
docs.text:
The XRM normalizer is invoked only after NOMAD has imported the upload and the archive parser has parsed the *.archive.yaml mainfile. Its implementation is located in:

packages/pynxtools-xrm/src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/schema_packages/schema.py

The converter starts at XRMDataConverter.normalize() and invokes convert_tomoproc() before registering the finished output through process_updated_raw_file():

report = convert_tomoproc(
    metadata,
    tiffs,
    output,
    compression=CompressionConfig(...),
    overwrite=True,
)

archive.m_context.process_updated_raw_file(self.output, allow_modify=True)

References:

  • XRMDataConverter.normalize() (src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/schema_packages/schema.py in the checkout)
  • convert_tomoproc() (src/pynxtools_xrm/streaming_writer.py in the checkout)

The recorded failing Temporal activity was update_files_activity, and its traceback ended in StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() while deleting the temporary source ZIP. It did not end in XRMDataConverter.normalize().

docs.title: Reprocess the upload
docs.text: For local development, manually starting Reprocess again works because the first attempt already copied the archive members into staging. This is useful for testing but should not be treated as a production solution.

docs.title: Use TAR instead of ZIP on Windows
docs.text:
Uploading a .tar or .tar.gz archive avoids the affected ZIP filesystem branch. NOMAD reads TAR input inside an explicit file context:

with target_fs.open(location, "rb") as file:
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=file, mode="r|*") as tar:
        ...

The file context is closed before cleanup attempts to remove the temporary archive.

docs.title: Run the development Oasis on Linux or WSL
docs.text: The intended production environment is Linux. Running the development worker inside Linux or WSL also avoids the immediate Windows unlink restriction. Explicitly closing the resource remains preferable because it avoids leaking a file descriptor.

docs.title: Proposed NOMAD-Core fix
docs.text:
The durable fix belongs in NOMAD Core's FSUtility._open_archive_fs(), not in pynxtools-xrm. The wrapper should always execute cleanup and should also close the owning OpenFile for a ZipFileSystem:

def _wrap(_fs):
    owner = getattr(_fs, "of", None)
    try:
        yield _fs
    finally:
        if hasattr(_fs, "close"):
            _fs.close()

        # ZipFileSystem.close() closes the ZipFile but, when constructed from
        # a path, the owner returned by fsspec.open() must also be closed.
        if isinstance(_fs, ZipFileSystem) and owner is not None:
            close_owner = getattr(owner, "close", None)
            if callable(close_owner):
                close_owner()

Before submitting this upstream, the patch should also be checked for ZIP write and append modes and for non-local filesystems. The fix must not prematurely close a caller-owned file object.

An alternative implementation is to make the ownership explicit when creating the ZipFileSystem: open the source file in an outer with block, construct the ZIP filesystem from that file object, and close the ZIP filesystem before leaving the outer block.

docs.title: Suggested regression test
docs.text:
A regression test should verify both the resource state and actual Windows deletion behavior. The resource assertion also catches the problem on Linux, where unlinking an open file would otherwise hide it.

import zipfile

from nomad.files import FSUtility


def test_open_archive_releases_source_file(tmp_path):
    archive_path = tmp_path / "upload.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path, "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr("metadata.json", "{}")

    with FSUtility.open_archive(str(archive_path)) as archive_fs:
        assert archive_fs.cat("metadata.json") == b"{}"
        source_file = archive_fs.fo

    # This assertion detects the leaked owner on every operating system.
    assert source_file.closed

    # On Windows this operation raised WinError 32 before the fix.
    archive_path.unlink()
    assert not archive_path.exists()

A second integration test can exercise StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() with cleanup_source_file_and_dir=True:

def test_add_rawfiles_removes_temporary_zip(staging_upload_files, tmp_path):
    archive_path = tmp_path / "upload.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path, "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr("metadata.json", "{}")

    staging_upload_files.add_rawfiles(
        str(archive_path),
        cleanup_source_file_and_dir=True,
        auto_decompress=True,
    )

    assert staging_upload_files.raw_path_exists("metadata.json")
    assert not archive_path.exists()

docs.title: Verification checklist
docs.text:
After applying a NOMAD-Core fix:

  1. Start the local Oasis on Windows.
  2. Upload a fresh ZIP containing an XRM *.archive.yaml, metadata JSON, and a small numbered TIFF stack.
  3. Confirm that update_files_activity completes successfully.
  4. Confirm that the temporary ZIP disappears from .volumes/fs/tmp.
  5. Confirm that the archive entry and generated .nxs entry both reach SUCCESS during the first workflow.
  6. Confirm that the .nxs volume retains its expected shape, dtype, chunks, and gzip compression.

docs.title: Scope decision for pynxtools-xrm
docs.text:
No workaround is currently added to XRMDataConverter, because:

  • the error occurs before the converter is invoked;
  • the target production Oasis runs on Linux;
  • changing the converter cannot release a file handle owned by NOMAD's upload layer;
  • the appropriate permanent correction is in NOMAD Core or fsspec resource handling.

This document records the issue so that it can be revisited if Windows becomes a supported deployment target or if the same resource leak appears in another environment.

docs.title: Supply additional metadata
docs.text: The converter merges image headers, associated recipe metadata, an assigned eLabFTW JSON export and explicit supplements. Supplements fill missing values; they must not replace values already supplied by the other sources. Preserve real measurement values rather than making conversion succeed with placeholders.

docs.title: Which values are required?
docs.text:
All targets require a sample name, theta and native stage X/Y/Z coordinates. The current XRM profile imposes some requirements in addition to NXDL validation. See the mapping reference for distinctions.

Target Additional metadata required by this converter TXRM / NXtomo Measured angle per projection; integer primary images; generated primary TXRM image_key=0 TXM / NXtomoproc Source type/name, reconstruction program/version/date, raw acquisition filename, positive cubic voxel size, verified image orientation; measured slice Y coordinates XRM / NXxrm_image Positive object-side pixel size; one image Reconstructed TIFF / NXtomoproc Same reconstruction fields, explicit voxel size, orientation and three-coordinate volume_origin_um; no measured TXM slice array available Projection TIFF / NXtomo Actual per-frame theta and integer role array image_key (0..3); integer primary images

The missing-fields exception reports unresolved values, not proof that no source contains the information. The reader currently decodes only selected TXM/RCP fields. The mappings can be extended after their meaning is established.

docs.title: Option 1: supplement a binary image using archive YAML
docs.text:
Save scan/reconstruction.archive.yaml in the same upload as the source. The following is a synthetic illustration; replace source and reconstruction values with verified records. Add only fields absent from the assigned sources.

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  input_file: scan/tomo-A/reconstruction.txm
  metadata_file: scan/measurement.json
  target_definition: NXtomoproc
  export: true
  metadata_supplements:
    source_type: "Fixed Tube X-ray"
    source_name: "Synthetic example tube"
    reconstruction_version: "1.0-example"
    reconstruction_date: "2026-08-26T12:00:00+02:00"
    image_orientation:
      row_axis: z
      column_axis: x
      row_sign: 1
      column_sign: 1

This matches a common five-field failure, assuming reconstruction_program, sample, geometry, voxel size and raw-file reference already exist. If a program name is also missing, add reconstruction_program with its true value. The quoted source_type is an example of a NeXus source category, not an arbitrary test string; check the enum in your active NXsource/NXDL definitions.

The input_file assignment is essential. Putting supplements in a TIFF-only YAML does not configure a TXM. metadata_file is relative to the upload root, not to the YAML. Once saved/uploaded, reprocess the full upload.

Do not add theta: 0 or zero stage coordinates when the image already supplies them. Different explicit values raise MetadataConflict. The same applies to units: supplement keys ending _um are numbers in micrometres, and theta is in degrees. A mismatching supplement does not “win” over the image.

docs.title: Option 2: provide an eLabFTW-style JSON export
docs.text:
The resolver reads exact, case-sensitive labels in metadata_decoded.extra_fields. This small synthetic JSON shows the five-field case, with orientation supplied as explicit configuration:

{
  "metadata_decoded": {
    "extra_fields": {
      "Source type": {"value": "Fixed Tube X-ray"},
      "Source name": {"value": "Synthetic example tube"},
      "Software version": {"value": "1.0-example"},
      "Reconstruction date": {"value": "2026-08-26T12:00:00+02:00"}
    }
  },
  "xrm_configuration": {
    "image_orientation": {
      "row_axis": "z",
      "column_axis": "x",
      "row_sign": 1,
      "column_sign": 1
    }
  }
}

For that example, assign the JSON to the binary with metadata_file, or put it as the sole eLabFTW-style JSON in the nearest measurement folder. It augments image/RCP values; it is not a complete metadata record for a bare TIFF stack.

JSON label / location Resolver key Expected value Source type source_type Source category supported by active NeXus definitions Source name source_name Actual radiation source designation Reconstruction software reconstruction_program Program used to reconstruct Software version reconstruction_version That program's version, as text Reconstruction date reconstruction_date Full date/time, preferably explicit UTC offset Sample name sample_name Measurement's sample identity Raw data path raw_file Actual source acquisition reference Reconstructed voxel size pixel_size_um Positive number plus explicit supported unit Stage X, Stage Y, Stage Z stage_x_um, stage_y_um, stage_z_um Number plus explicit length unit Top-level xrm_configuration.image_orientation image_orientation Axis mapping with integer signs

For example "Reconstructed voxel size": {"value": 500, "unit": "nm"} converts to pixel_size_um=0.5. Supported length units include nm, um, µm, μm, mm, cm, m. Not every field uses that same conversion: see metadata.read_elabftw_metadata and the mapping reference for field-specific units.

xrm_configuration accepts only theta, image_orientation, volume_origin_um and image_key. Do not place source_name or reconstruction keys there. Use the extra-field labels above or YAML metadata_supplements instead. Lab-book free text and differently named labels are not automatically interpreted. There is no live eLabFTW API lookup; upload the correct export and referenced metadata.

docs.title: Option 3: CLI supplements JSON
docs.text:
The CLI --supplements file is a plain object of resolver keys, not an eLabFTW export and not a NOMAD data: envelope. For the same synthetic case, save missing-values.json:

{
  "source_type": "Fixed Tube X-ray",
  "source_name": "Synthetic example tube",
  "reconstruction_version": "1.0-example",
  "reconstruction_date": "2026-08-26T12:00:00+02:00",
  "image_orientation": {
    "row_axis": "z", "column_axis": "x", "row_sign": 1, "column_sign": 1
  }
}

pynx-xrm convert --input scan/tomo-A/reconstruction.txm --metadata scan/measurement.json --supplements missing-values.json --output reconstruction.nxs

CLI paths are ordinary paths relative to the shell's current directory (unless absolute). They do not use NOMAD's upload-root convention. The CLI does not scan for NOMAD archive YAML or automatically discover sidecars: pass --metadata and repeatable --recipe explicitly as needed.

docs.title: Complete synthetic TIFF example
docs.text:
For a runnable miniature stack, use the bundled example's metadata.json and xrm.archive.yaml. In that example the metadata include sample, source, reconstruction program/version/date, raw reference, voxel size, stage coordinates and xrm_configuration for theta, origin and orientation. Its input is in layers/ and output is xrm_example.nxs. See the example README for the exact files.

For a projection TIFF job with three frames, actual measurement configuration would have the structure below; the angles and positions are synthetic:

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  tiff_directory: projections
  target_definition: NXtomo
  output: _nexus/projections.nxs
  export: true
  metadata_supplements:
    sample_name: "Synthetic projection example"
    theta: [0.0, 45.0, 90.0]
    stage_x_um: 0.0
    stage_y_um: 0.0
    stage_z_um: 0.0
    image_key: [0, 0, 0]

Only use measured angles and confirmed coordinates for real data. image_key must have one valid integer per frame. Additional NXDL-required content is checked against the definitions installed in your environment.

docs.title: Dates, orientation and precedence
docs.text:
Use quoted timestamps such as "2026-08-26T12:00:00+02:00". Full timestamps are required; a calendar date alone is insufficient for reconstruction time. Naive local timestamps are interpreted in Europe/Berlin; ambiguous or nonexistent DST times are rejected. The acquisition date, layer timestamp, conversion time and reconstruction time have different meanings.

For reconstructed volumes, row_axis: z and column_axis: x are required by the current model; row_sign and column_sign must each be integer 1 or -1. Confirm these from the reconstruction/export convention or calibration. They are not arbitrary switches to suppress errors. A TIFF volume also needs volume_origin_um: [x, y, z], the first voxel position in the model's sample frame. TXM instead uses measured slice positions and centred local X/Z axes.

Precedence is image > associated RCP > eLabFTW > explicit supplements. Conflicting lower-priority source values are recorded; a conflicting explicit supplement raises an error. RCP currently contributes sample name and, for reconstructions, acquisition reference. TXM exeVersion is preserved as file_software_version, not assumed to be reconstruction software version. Layer dates are preserved, not asserted to be reconstruction time. Extending those mappings requires verification of the manufacturer fields' semantics.

docs.title: Structure and process a NOMAD upload
docs.text: Automatic processing needs a configured server, supported image files, complete metadata and unambiguous associations. Directory layout alone cannot guarantee that arbitrary manufacturer files satisfy the supported profile. First complete Oasis deployment.

docs.title: Binary image upload
docs.text:
Upload the entire tree together, or a ZIP preserving the following structure. Here / is the upload raw-file root, not the server filesystem root:

/
└── scan/
    ├── measurement.json
    ├── recipe.rcp
    ├── reconstruction.archive.yaml
    └── tomo-A/
        ├── acquisition.txrm
        ├── reconstruction.txm
        └── FrontScoutImage.xrm

The names are illustrative. Keep original vendor basenames and acquisition directory names when possible: RCP association uses declared filenames and directory context. Recipe and eLabFTW JSON should describe these measurements. Each ZEISS image with supported headers is automatically matched by the binary parser. Without custom options, no YAML is required if the associated sources already provide every required value. A single-image XRM must contain one frame.

An example scan/reconstruction.archive.yaml is:

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  input_file: scan/tomo-A/reconstruction.txm
  metadata_file: scan/measurement.json
  recipe_file: scan/recipe.rcp
  target_definition: NXtomoproc
  export: true
  metadata_supplements:
    image_orientation:
      row_axis: z
      column_axis: x
      row_sign: 1
      column_sign: 1

This example assumes all other required metadata are available in the assigned sources and that the orientation has been verified. Use the full metadata examples when fields are missing. recipe_file is optional; if set it must still match the image. An explicit assignment does not bypass the association check.

docs.title: Path and configuration rules
docs.text:
1. Every input_file, metadata_file, recipe_file, tiff_directory and output path is relative to the upload root. A nested YAML does not change the base.
  2. Use / separators and exact filename case for Linux. Server-absolute and external paths are not accepted for input; paths must resolve inside the upload.
  3. A ZIP containing a top-level scan/ directory needs scan/... paths. A ZIP containing only its contents needs paths without that prefix. Inspect NOMAD's Files view after extraction before choosing a path.
  4. Use one *.archive.yaml per binary input. The parser scans the upload for matching data.input_file; duplicate matching jobs are an error. Filename similarity alone does not assign a YAML to a binary.
  5. For binary files use input_file. A YAML containing only tiff_directory configures a TIFF job and supplies no metadata to a TXM parser. Do not set both.
  6. Choose distinct output paths for different jobs. Retain the default for binary images unless an explicit naming convention is needed.

docs.title: Automatic sidecar discovery
docs.text:
For each binary source, the parser searches its directory, then ancestors up to the upload root. At the nearest level containing an eLabFTW-style JSON (a JSON object containing metadata_decoded), it uses that file. Two matching JSONs at that level are ambiguous: set metadata_file explicitly. An unrelated plain JSON supplement file is not automatically interpreted as eLabFTW metadata.

RCP discovery similarly selects the nearest directory containing .rcp files. The reader then requires an unambiguous association through RecipePoint file declarations or acquisition-directory context. An unrelated RCP in that scope can stop conversion; keep acquisitions in separate directories or explicitly assign the correct recipe. The reader does not merge all recipes or all JSON files in the upload.

docs.title: TIFF stack upload
docs.text:
TIFF images do not independently trigger the XRM volume converter. Upload a job:

/
├── volume.archive.yaml
├── metadata.json
└── layers/
    ├── layer_0001.tif
    ├── layer_0002.tif
    └── layer_0003.tif

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  tiff_directory: layers
  metadata_file: metadata.json
  target_definition: NXtomoproc
  output: _nexus/volume.nxs
  export: true

This requires a complete metadata JSON; the bundled synthetic example provides one. TIFF discovery is not recursive: all slices must be in layers/. Each file must be single-page grayscale, with identical dimensions and datatype. Filenames must end in a numeric index, with no duplicates or gaps; the starting index need not be zero. A reconstructed stack additionally needs voxel calibration, volume origin and verified orientation. Projection TIFFs use NXtomo, real measured angles and one image_key per frame. See metadata.

For TIFF jobs, assign metadata_file explicitly. The YAML TIFF path does not perform the binary parser's automatic JSON/RCP discovery; recipe_file is not passed through that TIFF conversion path.

docs.title: Processing and verification
docs.text:
1. Submit images, JSON/RCP and YAML together. Avoid triggering a large conversion while associated files are still being uploaded.
  2. Inspect the Entries tab. A completed project/upload can still contain failed entries. Open each failure's Logs and expand its exception.
  3. Expect a successful binary conversion entry and a generated .nxs entry processed by the configured NeXus parser. An RCP need not have its own entry.
  4. Inspect output paths and datasets, not just the existence of an older .nxs file. Failed replacement preserves an older result.
  5. After adding/changing JSON, RCP or YAML, reprocess the entire upload. There is no custom sidecar watcher that automatically reruns dependent images.

For a small first check use NOMAD's installed XRM example upload. Its values are synthetic. Passing that example verifies the pipeline, not a real measurement's metadata accuracy. See troubleshooting for specific failures.

docs.title: Deploy on NOMAD 2.0.0 Oasis
docs.text: This guide addresses a Linux Oasis with separate application and processing workers. Adapt service names and paths to your installation. All examples use /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions as a chosen container/service path, not a NOMAD default. Keep app, worker, plugin, pynxtools and definition versions consistent.

docs.title: Files to change
docs.text:
File or setting Required change Purpose Distribution dependency file / image build (pyproject.toml, requirements or Dockerfile) Install the reviewed pynxtools-xrm version in app and worker environments; retain the distribution's NOMAD pin Registers parser, schema, app and example entry points Dockerfile.xrm (container example below) Install the wheel and run pynx-xrm definitions Provides the custom XML and complete base definitions inside the image docker-compose.override.yml or the actual Compose file Use the same prepared image for every Python app/worker service; set NEXUS_DEF_PATH Makes definitions visible to all processes Alternatively /etc/nomad/xrm.env and systemd drop-ins Set the absolute overlay path and load the environment file in each service Persists the variable outside interactive shells Existing nomad.yaml plugin configuration, only if filtering plugins Permit this plugin's entry points and the installed pynxtools NeXus parser Avoids installed-but-disabled plugins Upload *.archive.yaml / JSON Assign image paths and genuine missing metadata Configures a measurement, not the server

No change to installed third-party NXDL files is needed. The plugin's src/pynxtools_xrm/definitions.py implements overlay preparation; normally you run its CLI rather than editing that source file.

docs.title: Install into the actual processing environment
docs.text:
Installing on the host, in a different virtual environment or only in the web container does not update a worker. For an existing development checkout:

# Run using the intended virtual environment's python.
python -m pip install -e /path/to/pynxtools-xrm
pynx-xrm definitions --output /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions

For deployment use a reviewed wheel or pinned revision, with a reproducible image/dependency lock. If the distribution has an explicit plugin allow-list, merge the following installed entry points into that existing configuration:

pynxtools_xrm.nomad.parsers:xrm_raw_parser
pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages:xrm_data_converter
pynxtools_xrm.nomad.apps:xrm_app
pynxtools_xrm.nomad.example_uploads:xrm_example_upload

The first two are needed for binary and YAML conversion. The search app and example upload are optional. The generated .nxs also needs the distribution's active pynxtools NeXus parser. Do not replace an existing allow-list with only these four entries. The plugin's search app targets legacy parser field paths; successful conversion does not establish search-app compatibility with v2 paths.

For NOMAD's plugins.entry_points.include setting, the entries to merge into an existing nomad.yaml list have this form (retain all existing required entries, especially the distribution's NeXus parser):

plugins:
  entry_points:
    include:
      # Keep the existing entries here as well.
      - pynxtools_xrm.nomad.parsers:xrm_raw_parser
      - pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages:xrm_data_converter
      - pynxtools_xrm.nomad.apps:xrm_app
      - pynxtools_xrm.nomad.example_uploads:xrm_example_upload

Also check that no exclude rule disables these entries. If you already enable all installed plugins, no include-list change is required. NEXUS_DEF_PATH is a process environment variable, not a new top-level key to add to nomad.yaml.

docs.title: Docker: build definitions into the image
docs.text:
From the plugin repository, build a wheel in a build environment:

python -m pip install build
python -m build --wheel

Save this example as Dockerfile.xrm in that repository. Choose the exact base image already used by your Oasis. The same resulting image must serve all app and worker roles that import this plugin. Use an appropriate non-root runtime user if your base image defines one; the shown root user is for installation.

ARG NOMAD_BASE_IMAGE
FROM ${NOMAD_BASE_IMAGE}
USER root
COPY dist/*.whl /tmp/xrm-wheels/
RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir /tmp/xrm-wheels/*.whl
RUN pynx-xrm definitions --output /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions
ENV NEXUS_DEF_PATH=/opt/nomad/xrm-definitions
# Restore your base image's runtime USER here, if applicable.

The base image must resolve the declared pynxtools dependency without breaking its NOMAD distribution. Check the build and python -m pip check; do not bypass dependency conflicts. Use a fresh destination if that path already contains an unrecognized definitions tree.

Build with the base-image tag used by your installation:

docker build --build-arg NOMAD_BASE_IMAGE=YOUR_EXISTING_PINNED_NOMAD_IMAGE -f Dockerfile.xrm -t nomad-oasis-xrm:local .

In the directory containing the Oasis Compose files, add or merge docker-compose.override.yml. Replace app and worker with actual service names from docker compose config --services; add equivalent settings for every additional worker. Existing commands, volumes and settings remain needed.

services:
  app:
    image: nomad-oasis-xrm:local
    environment:
      NEXUS_DEF_PATH: /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions
  worker:
    image: nomad-oasis-xrm:local
    environment:
      NEXUS_DEF_PATH: /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions

Inspect the merged configuration, then recreate the affected services using your actual names. A restart alone does not apply a changed Compose environment.

docker compose config
docker compose up -d --force-recreate app worker

Alternatively prepare definitions using the same package versions in a host directory and mount the whole tree read-only into every relevant service:

volumes:
  - ./xrm-definitions:/opt/nomad/xrm-definitions:ro
environment:
  NEXUS_DEF_PATH: /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions

This fragment belongs inside each service. The host directory must already contain the prepared tree. A mount over an image's definition directory hides that image content, so do not accidentally mount an empty directory over it.

docs.title: Native Linux services: systemd alternative
docs.text:
Prepare definitions with the same virtual environment used by the services. Ensure service users can traverse and read the full tree. Create /etc/nomad/xrm.env with:

NEXUS_DEF_PATH=/opt/nomad/xrm-definitions

For each actual unit, use systemctl edit UNIT_NAME to add a drop-in such as /etc/systemd/system/UNIT_NAME.service.d/override.conf:

[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/etc/nomad/xrm.env

Replace UNIT_NAME with the application and each worker unit. Run systemctl daemon-reload and restart those units during an appropriate service window. An interactive shell export is not inherited by existing systemd services. Use the equivalent persistent environment mechanism if using another process manager.

docs.title: Verify inside each app and worker environment
docs.text:
For Docker, prefix these commands with docker compose exec SERVICE_NAME and use the actual Python interpreter used by that service:

python -m pip check
python -c 'import os, sys; from importlib.metadata import version; print(sys.executable); print(version("pynxtools-xrm")); print(version("pynxtools")); print(os.environ.get("NEXUS_DEF_PATH"))'
python -c 'from pynxtools.nexus.utils import get_nxdl_root_and_path; print(get_nxdl_root_and_path("NXxrm_image")[1]); print(get_nxdl_root_and_path("NXtomoproc")[1]); print(get_nxdl_root_and_path("NXtomo")[1])'
python -c 'from importlib.metadata import entry_points; print([e.name for e in entry_points(group="nomad.plugin") if e.value.startswith("pynxtools_xrm.")])'

Expect NXxrm_image to resolve to /opt/nomad/xrm-definitions/applications/NXxrm_image.nxdl.xml, and the standard applications to the same tree. Entry-point enumeration proves installation, not that an allow-list enabled them. Check the deployment's plugin information and worker logs as well. A new exec process confirms the container environment; the running workers must also have been recreated/restarted with it.

Process the bundled synthetic example, then a representative TXRM/TXM/XRM upload. Check the binary entries and their generated NeXus entries. Reprocess an existing affected upload after fixing the server setup.

docs.title: Definition files and upgrades
docs.text:
Location Meaning site-packages/pynxtools/definitions/applications/ Standard installed application definitions site-packages/pynxtools_xrm/definitions/applications/NXxrm_image.nxdl.xml Plugin source of the custom single-image definition $NEXUS_DEF_PATH/applications/NXxrm_image.nxdl.xml Active copied custom definition $NEXUS_DEF_PATH/xrm-overlay.json Base revision and custom-definition checksum recorded during preparation

Find the installed plugin XML without guessing the Python version:

python -c 'from pathlib import Path; import pynxtools_xrm; print(Path(pynxtools_xrm.__file__).parent / "definitions/applications/NXxrm_image.nxdl.xml")'

NEXUS_DEF_PATH points to the root containing applications, base_classes and related definition files. It is not the XML filename or the plugin's private applications directory. pynxtools captures the path during import.

The overlay command copies the installed pynxtools definitions and adds only NXxrm_image. It refuses an existing destination without its marker, and refuses reusing a marked tree with a different base revision. After an upgrade, create a fresh versioned directory, point all processes to it, restart them and repeat the lookup and conversion checks. Prepare the overlay before switching NEXUS_DEF_PATH; stale environment settings can affect imports.

The optional packaged XML is named NXxrm_tomoproc, extending NXtomoproc. It is not copied by this command and is not an accepted YAML/CLI target. TXM conversion uses NXtomoproc; copying or renaming the optional XML alone does not enable another target. Additional optional domain metadata are emitted by the mapping code. Supporting a new target requires coordinated reader, mapping, writer, schema and validation changes and tests.

docs.title: Upstream guidance
docs.text: Use the NOMAD documentation for the distribution's installation, plugin and administration procedures. This guide documents the extra requirements of the ZBT plugin, not a replacement Oasis deployment.

docs.title: Diagnose conversion failures
docs.text:
Open the failed entry's Logs and expand the exception. Record the processing time and mainfile: an older failure or a generated NeXus entry can describe a different stage from the binary conversion you are investigating.

Error / symptom Cause to check Action The nxdl file, NXxrm_image, was not found Overlay missing or invisible in the worker; variable set after import Prepare complete overlay; persist NEXUS_DEF_PATH in every app/worker; recreate/restart; verify inside worker MissingRequiredMetadata Unresolved profile fields Read exact field list; assign correct JSON/RCP; supply genuine missing values Same missing fields after adding YAML YAML has no matching input_file, incorrect extension/name or reprocessing not run Use *.archive.yaml, full upload-relative image path, one matching job; reprocess upload FileNotFoundError for metadata/input Nested YAML paths treated as YAML-relative; ZIP prefix or case differs Compare against upload Files tree; use upload-root-relative paths Multiple YAML jobs refer to the same binary input Duplicate matching configuration Keep one matching job per binary input Multiple eLabFTW files Two candidate JSONs in nearest metadata scope Set metadata_file explicitly RCP not unambiguously associated Recipe declarations/context do not match image Preserve vendor tree; select correct recipe; verify actual relationship MetadataConflict / Explicit ... cannot override ... Supplement differs from an existing source value Remove redundant supplement; correct authoritative source if it is wrong Full timestamp / DST error Date-only or ambiguous local time Supply actual full timestamp with explicit UTC offset Orientation error Missing or unsupported row/column convention Confirm axes, use row=z, column=x and signs ±1; do not guess Slice spacing conflicts with cubic calibration TXM Y spacing disagrees with voxel size Check original calibration/headers; do not force a replacement voxel size TIFF numbering / dimensions / grayscale error Gaps, duplicate indices, multipage/color images or inconsistent slices Correct the input stack; see upload requirements Existing destination has no overlay marker / base changed Unsafe overlay reuse Prepare a new directory from the current environment; switch processes together Another conversion targets the same output Concurrent jobs or a stale lock after termination Ensure distinct output names; verify no active writer before administrator recovery Conversion succeeds but .nxs entry fails Generated-file parser/schema setup Inspect that entry's logs, enabled NeXus parser and definition paths Search app does not show converted entries App uses legacy NeXus parser fields Inspect generated archive and parser version; do not infer conversion failure from the app Upload says completed but entries failed Aggregate status differs from entry result Check each conversion and generated NeXus entry

Do not fix missing source type, version or orientation with arbitrary Test values or zero coordinates. Successful conversion is not evidence of physical correctness. Refer to metadata examples.

After changing metadata or definitions, restart services when required and reprocess the upload. An older .nxs can remain after a failed replacement; check the latest entry log and status. See output lifecycle.

For Windows ZIP extraction locks before parsing begins, see the separate Windows import note. It is not the same problem as Linux NXDL lookup or missing measurement metadata.

docs.title: Information for a bug report
docs.text: Use the project issue tracker or contact the maintainer. Include package revision, Python, NOMAD and pynxtools versions; affected file type; complete relevant exception; an anonymized directory tree and YAML/JSON example; and definition lookup output from the actual worker. Describe expected and actual behavior. Share a minimal reproducer when permitted; remove credentials and confidential experiment data.

docs.title: Versions and reproducibility
docs.text:
The distribution version comes from setuptools-scm and Git history at build time. Query installed versions in the actual worker environment:

python -c 'from importlib.metadata import version; print("pynxtools-xrm", version("pynxtools-xrm")); print("pynxtools", version("pynxtools")); print("nomad-lab", version("nomad-lab"))'

The NOMAD query requires NOMAD to be installed; standalone conversion does not. Record the Git revision for editable installations as well as the reported version. Do not infer the deployed worker revision from a local checkout.

The converter records its package name, version and actual conversion time in /entry/conversion (NXprocess). The reconstruction software/version/date in /entry/reconstruction describe the experimental processing and are independent of the converter's version/time. A TXM file's exeVersion is retained as source metadata rather than silently substituted for either quantity.

The overlay marker xrm-overlay.json records the base-definition revision and NXxrm_image checksum. Keep it with the deployment configuration. Rebuild a fresh overlay when upgrading the base definitions and switch app/workers together. See deployment.

For reproducibility retain original files, RCP, uploaded JSON, configuration, package/image revision, definitions and generated NeXus. Output reuse considers source file stamps, metadata and implementation fingerprint; see outputs. It does not establish that a source file was unchanged if external software modified bytes while preserving size and mtime.

docs.title: NOMAD archive YAML
docs.text:
Use UTF-8 files named *.archive.yaml with a data: object and:

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
data field Type / default Meaning input_file string; absent Binary TXRM/TXM/XRM path relative to upload root; selects binary ownership tiff_directory string; absent TIFF slice directory relative to upload root; use when no input_file metadata_file string; absent eLabFTW-style JSON path relative to upload root recipe_file string; absent Explicit RCP path for binary processing; not forwarded by TIFF YAML path target_definition enum NXtomo, NXtomoproc, NXxrm_image; inferred from binary extension, TIFF defaults to NXtomoproc metadata_supplements JSON object; absent Resolver keys for missing values; see metadata guide output string Binary default _nexus/<relative source>.nxs; TIFF fallback xrm_volume.nxs gzip_level integer; 4 gzip compression level, 0..9 target_chunk_mib number; 1.0 Target uncompressed chunk size in MiB; must give a positive valid configuration export boolean; true Enables YAML normalizer conversion/request; generated binary sections set it to false internally assumptions legacy list of strings Retained schema field; does not fabricate missing required values conversion_status generated string requested, converted or reused; not user input nexus_view generated archive reference Link to generated NeXus entry; not user input

export: false stops the YAML normalizer. It does not disable the independent binary matching parser or make it ignore a matching YAML's options. Use the deployment's processing controls when disabling a parser is intended.

The target must match a binary's type: TXRM → NXtomo, TXM → NXtomoproc, XRM → NXxrm_image. TIFF supports only NXtomo and NXtomoproc. The packaged optional NXxrm_tomoproc is not selectable.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
pynx-xrm inspect INPUT
pynx-xrm definitions --output DIRECTORY
pynx-xrm convert (--input IMAGE | --tiffs DIRECTORY) --output FILE.nxs [OPTIONS]
Convert option Meaning --metadata FILE One eLabFTW-style JSON --recipe FILE RCP; repeatable, association must be unambiguous --supplements FILE Plain JSON object containing resolver keys --target NAME Same three allowed targets as above --gzip-level N Default 4 --chunk-mib SIZE Default 1.0 --overwrite Allow validated replacement/reuse of an existing output

CLI sidecars are explicit; NOMAD's automatic folder discovery and YAML scanning are not run. inspect reports image dimensions, frame count, datatype and auxiliary block names, or recipe information for RCP. It does not print every decoded image metadata field and does not replace full conversion validation.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: NEXUS_DEF_PATH selects the complete NeXus definitions root and must be set before Python imports. Read the deployment guide for persistent Compose/systemd examples and verification commands.

docs.title: Bundled synthetic example
docs.text:
NOMAD's XRM example-upload entry point supplies a tiny reconstructed TIFF job. Its resources are located at src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/example_uploads/example/ in the checkout:

/
├── README.md
├── xrm.archive.yaml
├── metadata.json
└── layers/
    └── numbered grayscale TIFF slices

The YAML references metadata.json and layers relative to that upload root, uses NXtomoproc, and writes xrm_example.nxs. The JSON contains the complete synthetic source/reconstruction metadata, voxel size and geometry. All values are artificial and must not be copied into a real measurement.

Load the installed XRM example through NOMAD's example-project/upload feature, or upload the contents of the example directory preserving layers/. An extra enclosing folder changes the upload root paths and requires adjusting the YAML. Process the YAML and inspect both its result and the generated NeXus entry. The configuration reference explains these fields.

The example validates the reconstruction pipeline; separately test a real single-image XRM to verify NXxrm_image lookup and the installed NeXus parser.

docs.title: NOMAD binary defaults
docs.text:
The automatic binary parser writes one NeXus file per source image. Given a source path relative to the upload root, the default is:

_nexus/<relative parent directories>/<original filename including extension>.nxs
Source in upload Default generated file in upload acquisition.txrm _nexus/acquisition.txrm.nxs scan/tomo-A/acquisition.txrm _nexus/scan/tomo-A/acquisition.txrm.nxs scan/tomo-A/reconstruction.txm _nexus/scan/tomo-A/reconstruction.txm.nxs scan/tomo-A/FrontScoutImage.xrm _nexus/scan/tomo-A/FrontScoutImage.xrm.nxs

Keeping .txrm, .txm or .xrm in the output name avoids collisions between different input types sharing a stem. _nexus is a plugin naming convention inside the upload, not a directory to create under the server's installation.

Override with data.output: results/reconstruction.nxs in the matching binary YAML. The path is relative to the upload root and must stay inside it. Use a separate .nxs filename and never target an input. Different jobs must not share outputs. A subsequent output-name change can leave the previous result in the upload; it is not automatically renamed or removed.

docs.title: TIFF and CLI outputs
docs.text:
TIFF YAML jobs use exactly data.output, relative to the upload root; the fallback when omitted is xrm_volume.nxs at the upload root, not a path under _nexus. Set an explicit unique output for every TIFF job. The bundled example uses xrm_example.nxs.

The CLI requires --output. It resolves relative paths against the working directory and does not add _nexus or the original extension automatically. Existing output requires --overwrite for CLI conversion; NOMAD requests overwrite through its conversion adapter.

docs.title: HDF5 dataset paths
docs.text:
Application Primary pixel dataset Array order NXtomo /entry/instrument/detector/data (linked as /entry/data/data) projection, column, row NXtomoproc /entry/data/data x, y-layer, z NXxrm_image /entry/instrument/detector/data (linked as /entry/image/image_2d/intensity) row, column

Projection frames and reconstruction slices are transposed during streaming to the documented target order. XRM retains its row/column image layout. Physical axes, geometry and metadata accompany the pixels. These internal HDF5 paths are not upload filenames and must not be used as YAML output paths.

docs.title: NOMAD entries, status and reuse
docs.text:
The binary mainfile owns conversion; the YAML requests processing of that mainfile. Its conversion_status: requested does not prove that conversion has finished. Successful binary entries report converted or reused. A TIFF YAML owns its own conversion. Newly written .nxs files are submitted to the configured pynxtools NeXus parser as separate mainfiles. nexus_view links the converter to the generated archive's data; it is not another raw data file.

Check both conversion and generated NeXus entry status. A generated file can exist while its NeXus parsing fails. An unchanged validated output can be reused without requesting generated-file processing again; if only the NeXus parser configuration changed, explicitly reprocess that generated entry as well.

Writes use gzip compression, an exclusive output lock, a temporary .part file and atomic replacement after validation. Failed conversion preserves an older valid output, so file existence alone does not prove the latest run succeeded. Reuse checks source path/size/mtime, effective metadata, recipe, compression, application NXDL and implementation fingerprint. It does not reread the complete input pixel content for cache lookup. The pixel checksum is computed while writing.

docs.title: Develop and contribute
docs.text: The plugin is developed at ZBT by Jonas Fortmann. Contributions should preserve measurement semantics, document new mappings and include focused validation. See contact for ownership and upstream attribution.

docs.title: Development environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jonasdfortmann/pynxtools-xrm.git
cd pynxtools-xrm
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[dev,docs]'
pynx-xrm definitions --output "$PWD/run/xrm-definitions"
export NEXUS_DEF_PATH="$PWD/run/xrm-definitions"
pre-commit install

For NOMAD integration use the distribution's development environment and install this checkout there; use its NOMAD version pin. The optional nomad extra is available when NOMAD is not already supplied. Do not import the package before setting the definitions path in the Python process under test.

docs.title: Source map
docs.text: File Responsibility src/pynxtools_xrm/zeiss.py ZEISS headers, frame iterator, RCP matching src/pynxtools_xrm/tiff_stack.py Numbered stack discovery and iteration src/pynxtools_xrm/metadata.py, elabftw.py Resolution, precedence, ELN labels and provenance src/pynxtools_xrm/mapping.py, geometry.py NeXus fields and coordinate transforms src/pynxtools_xrm/streaming_writer.py Metadata Writer, pixel streaming, validation and atomic output src/pynxtools_xrm/definitions.py Explicit full definitions overlay src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/jobs.py Upload-relative paths and sidecar associations src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/parsers/parser.py Binary owner conversion and generated file registration src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/schema_packages/schema.py YAML adapter and TIFF jobs

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run checks applicable to the changed code:

ruff check src tests
ruff format --check src tests
pytest tests

Some integration tests require NOMAD and suitable data. Review the test's setup before interpreting an unavailable integration environment as a plugin failure. Add tests for new decoded manufacturer fields, unit handling, ambiguous sidecars, orientation and actual output datasets. Do not substitute guessed metadata for missing experimental values. Keep one-image-at-a-time pixel memory behavior.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e '.[docs]'
mkdocs build --strict
mkdocs serve

Edit Markdown under docs/ and navigation in mkdocs.yaml. Separate tutorials, task guides, explanations and reference, following the NOMAD documentation structure. Keep repository metadata in README.md, pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff and docs/contact.md consistent. Use ZBT/Jonas Fortmann authorship; retain genuine upstream copyright notices in derived template code. Do not copy upstream funding or maintenance claims into this project's citation metadata.

Every example must state its path base and distinguish synthetic values from measurement data. Validate YAML/JSON and check examples against the current schema and sidecar behavior. Update supported targets, output paths and failure instructions together when implementation changes.

Submit a focused pull request to the project repository with the problem, behavior change and validation. For a mapping extension, explain why the source field represents that quantity, including units and format/version limitations. Coordinate changes to upstream pynxtools or NOMAD with their own maintainers.

docs.title: Install pynxtools-xrm
docs.text: This tutorial installs the converter into an isolated Python environment and checks its NeXus definitions. For NOMAD 2.0.0 Oasis deployment, continue with the server guide; a local installation does not install the plugin into a remote worker.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >=3.10; the examples use Python 3.12.
  • pynxtools>=0.15.2,<0.16, installed by the package dependency resolver.
  • Disk space for the input and compressed output, including a temporary new output alongside an existing result during replacement.
  • For NOMAD: the plugin and the configured pynxtools NeXus parser in the app and worker environments. The package declares a NOMAD extra, but its dependency lower bound is not a compatibility guarantee for all NOMAD releases.

docs.title: Install from the repository
docs.text:
Use the ZBT developer's repository. Pin a reviewed tag or commit for deployment; do not assume the moving default branch is a stable release.

git clone https://github.com/jonasdfortmann/pynxtools-xrm.git
cd pynxtools-xrm
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .

On Windows, activate with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell. If NOMAD is not already provided by your development environment, install the optional extra with python -m pip install -e '.[nomad]'. An existing Oasis should retain its distribution's pinned NOMAD version; build and test the plugin into that image.

docs.title: Prepare NeXus definitions
docs.text:
The plugin ships NXxrm_image, but pynxtools does not automatically discover the plugin's private XML directory. Prepare a separate complete definitions tree:

pynx-xrm definitions --output "$PWD/run/xrm-definitions"
export NEXUS_DEF_PATH="$PWD/run/xrm-definitions"

PowerShell equivalent:

pynx-xrm definitions --output run/xrm-definitions
$env:NEXUS_DEF_PATH = (Resolve-Path run/xrm-definitions).Path

The output includes base classes, standard applications and the local applications/NXxrm_image.nxdl.xml. Set the variable before imports. Restart already running Python sessions after changing it. See the definition lifecycle for upgrades and the inactive NXxrm_tomoproc extension.

docs.title: Verify the environment
docs.text:
python -c 'from importlib.metadata import version; print(version("pynxtools-xrm")); print(version("pynxtools"))'
python -c 'from pynxtools.nexus.utils import get_nxdl_root_and_path; print(get_nxdl_root_and_path("NXxrm_image")[1]); print(get_nxdl_root_and_path("NXtomoproc")[1])'
pynx-xrm --help

Both XML lookups should resolve into the chosen overlay. This validates lookup, not a complete measurement. Next use genuine data or the bundled synthetic example, following the upload guide.
